title: Although, despite, without
seoTitle: Although and despite in Turkish: rağmen, hâlde
intro: This unit is about things that happen against the odds. `-DIğI hâlde` and `-mAsInA rağmen` both mean **although**: *Bildiği hâlde söylemedi*, *Yorgun olmasına rağmen çalıştı*. `-mAksIzIn` is the formal **without**: *Durmaksızın konuştu*. And a handful of link words set two sentences against each other: *ise*, *oysa*, *hâlbuki*, *buna rağmen*, *gerçi … ama*.

blocks.text: `-DIğI hâlde` means **although**: *Bildiği hâlde söylemedi* (Although he knew, he didn't say). It is the object participle of [B1 unit 6](gp-participle-dik) with its possessive, followed by *hâlde*, **in the state**: literally **in the state of having known**. The clause states a fact, and the main clause goes against it, often with surprise or reproach.

blocks.title: *bilmek*: although I know, although I knew

blocks.text: **Tense.** `-DIğI hâlde` covers the present and the past; the main clause sets the time: *Hasta olduğu hâlde işe gitti* (Although she was ill, she went to work), *Hasta olduğu hâlde işe gidiyor* (Although she's ill, she's going to work). For something still to come, use `-(y)AcAğI hâlde`: *Yarın sınavı olacağı hâlde hiç çalışmıyor* (Although he has an exam tomorrow, he isn't studying at all).

**Negatives, nouns and var.** The negative is `-mAdIğI hâlde`: *Hiç çalışmadığı hâlde sınavı geçti*. Nouns and adjectives go through *olmak*, and *var* and *yok* become *olduğu* and *olmadığı*: *Param olduğu hâlde almadım* (Although I had the money, I didn't buy it).

head: Kind
Example
Meaning
rows: although he has an exam coming
although I'm tired, I was tired
although I have, had the money
although I don't, didn't have time

blocks.text: **The subject.** A noun subject usually stays in the nominative, as in the time and reason clauses of [B1 unit 8](gp-digi-icin): *Annem istemediği hâlde gittim* (I went, although my mother didn't want me to).

items.en: Although he knew, he didn't say.
Although she was ill, she went to work.
Although he didn't study at all, he passed the exam.
Although you'd promised, you didn't come.
I went, although my mother didn't want me to.
Although I had the money, I didn't buy it.

blocks.text: Write *hâlde* with a circumflex, as TDK writes *hâl* (state): *bildiği hâlde*. In print you will often see *halde* without it.

blocks.title: Other uses of hâlde
blocks.text: After an adjective, *hâlde* is just **in a state**: *yorgun bir hâlde eve geldi* (she came home exhausted). *O hâlde* means **in that case, then**: *O hâlde yarın görüşelim* (Then let's meet tomorrow).

`-DIğI hâlde` states a fact; `-sA bile` ([B2 unit 1](gp-even-if)) imagines one. *Yağmur yağdığı hâlde gittik* (It was raining, and we went anyway) against *Yağmur yağsa bile gideriz* (We'll go even if it rains).

*Rağmen* (despite) takes the dative ([A2 unit 9](gp-postp-dative)): *yağmura rağmen* (despite the rain), *her şeye rağmen* (despite everything). To put a whole clause before it, turn the clause into a verbal noun in `-mA` with its possessive ([B1 unit 4](gp-ma-possessive)), then add the dative: *Yorgun olmasına rağmen çalıştı* (Although she was tired, she worked; literally **despite her being tired**).

blocks.title: *olmak*: although I am, although I was

blocks.text: The order never changes: stem, `-mA`, possessive, the n of the third person ([A1 unit 10](gp-pronominal-n)), dative, *rağmen*. In the negative, `-mA` comes twice: *çalışmamasına rağmen* (although he didn't work).

**No tense of its own.** *Yağmur yağmasına rağmen* means **although it rains, was raining or rained**; the main clause sets the time. For something still to come, use *olmak* after the future: *gelecek olmasına rağmen* (although he's going to come).

**The subject.** A noun subject normally takes the genitive, as with every `-mA` clause: *Havanın soğuk olmasına rağmen denize girdik* (Although the weather was cold, we went into the sea). Set phrases like *yağmur yağmak* keep the nominative: *Yağmur yağmasına rağmen*.

items.tr: Yorgun olmasına rağmen çalışmaya devam etti.
items.seg: Yorgun ol|ma|s|ı|n|a rağmen çalışmaya devam etti.
items.en: Although she was tired, she kept working.
Despite the rain, the match was played.
Although I studied hard, I couldn't pass the exam.

items.tr: Pahalı olmasına rağmen herkes o lokantaya gidiyor.
items.seg: Pahalı ol|ma|s|ı|n|a rağmen herkes o lokantaya gidiyor.
items.en: Although it's expensive, everyone goes to that restaurant.
Despite everything, we're happy.

items.tr: Yaşlı olmalarına karşın her gün yürüyüş yapıyorlar.
items.seg: Yaşlı ol|ma|ları|n|a karşın her gün yürüyüş yapıyorlar.
items.en: Although they're old, they go for a walk every day.

blocks.text: **-mAsInA rağmen or -DIğI hâlde?** Both translate **although**. `-mAsInA rağmen` is neutral and very common in writing and the news; `-DIğI hâlde` sounds more personal and often carries surprise or blame: *Söz verdiğin hâlde gelmedin!* The formal *karşın* can replace *rağmen*: *yorgun olmasına karşın*.

Like French **malgré**, *rağmen* takes a noun: **malgré la pluie**, *yağmura rağmen*. For a whole clause French switches to **bien que**; Turkish keeps *rağmen* and turns the clause into a noun: *yağmur yağmasına rağmen*.

`-mAksIzIn` means **without** doing something: *Hiç durmaksızın konuştu* (He talked without stopping). It is the formal partner of `-mAdAn` ([B1 unit 7](gp-madan)): you'll meet it in writing, the news and official notices, and in a few everyday words such as *durmaksızın* (nonstop).

blocks.caption: Everyday and formal
head: Everyday
Formal
Meaning
rows: He went in without asking permission.

blocks.text: **Only without.** `-mAdAn` also means **before** (*yatmadan önce*); `-mAksIzIn` never does. It has no persons and no negative: the subject comes from the main clause, or from a noun in front of it: *Kimse fark etmeksizin içeri girdi* (He came in without anyone noticing).

**Notices and rules.** Official texts like it: *Ziyaretçiler izin almaksızın kazı alanına giremez* (Visitors may not enter the excavation site without permission). In conversation the same sentence uses `-mAdAn`: *İzin almadan kazı alanına giremezsiniz*.

items.en: He talked without stopping.
They worked all night without sleeping.

items.tr: Ziyaretçiler izin almaksızın kazı alanına giremez.
items.seg: Ziyaretçiler izin al|maksızın kazı alanına giremez.
items.en: Visitors may not enter the excavation site without permission.
She left the city without telling anyone.
He came in without anyone noticing.

blocks.text: Inside `-mAksIzIn` you can see the infinitive `-mAk` and `-sIz`, **without** ([A2 unit 12](gp-siz)): literally **doing-less**. That's why it has only two forms, *-maksızın* and *-meksizin*.

sections.title: İse, oysa, hâlbuki, gerçi: setting things against each other

blocks.text: You know *ama* and *fakat* (but) and *yine de* (still, [A2 unit 11](gp-sequence-connectors)). These link words add **whereas**, **yet in fact**, **despite this** and **granted …, but**.

head: Word
Meaning
Example
rows: whereas, as for (after the word it contrasts)
*Herkes onu zengin sanıyor, oysa hiç parası yok.*
but in fact, whereas (often with reproach)
*Çok yorgunduk. Buna rağmen yürümeye devam ettik.*

blocks.text: **İse** is the *ise* of formal conditionals ([B1 unit 9](gp-conditional-real)) used as **as for, whereas**. It comes right after the word it contrasts, never at the start of the clause: *Ali İzmir'de oturuyor, kardeşi ise Ankara'da* (Ali lives in Izmir, whereas his brother lives in Ankara). Written apart it never changes; attached, it becomes `-(y)sA`: *kardeşiyse*.

**Oysa** (also *oysaki*) and **hâlbuki** open a clause that contradicts what came before, or what was expected. They are close; *hâlbuki* is more often a reproach: *Hâlbuki sana söylemiştim* (But I had told you).

**Gerçi** concedes a point, and *ama* or *fakat* follows: *Gerçi yorgunum, ama seninle gelirim* (I'm tired, it's true, but I'll come with you). Put second, *gerçi* means **though**: *Çok güzel bir ev, gerçi biraz küçük* (It's a lovely house, though a bit small).

items.tr: Ali İzmir'de oturuyor, kardeşi ise Ankara'da.
items.en: Ali lives in Izmir, whereas his brother lives in Ankara.

items.tr: Herkes onu zengin sanıyor, oysa hiç parası yok.
items.en: Everyone thinks he's rich, yet he has no money at all.
Why didn't you come? You had promised.

items.tr: Çok yorgunduk. Buna rağmen yürümeye devam ettik.
items.en: We were very tired. Despite this, we kept walking.
I'm tired, it's true, but I'll come with you.

blocks.text: *İse* follows the word it contrasts. *Ben çay içtim, ise Ayşe kahve içti* is wrong: *Ayşe ise kahve içti*.
*Oysa* and *hâlbuki* are close to French **alors que** and **pourtant**; *gerçi … ama* to **certes …, mais**.

summary: `-DIğI hâlde` is **although**, with the possessive of the doer: *bildiğim hâlde*, *bildikleri hâlde*; it states a fact, often with surprise or reproach.
Nouns, adjectives and *var* go through *olmak*: *hasta olduğu hâlde*, *param olduğu hâlde*.
`-mAsInA rağmen` is the neutral **although, despite**: *olmama, olmana, olmasına, olmamıza, olmanıza, olmalarına rağmen*; formal *karşın*. With a noun: *yağmura rağmen*, *her şeye rağmen*.
`-mAksIzIn` is the formal **without**: *durmaksızın*, *izin almaksızın*; it never means **before**.
*İse* (whereas) follows the word it contrasts: *Ayşe ise kahve içti*.
*Oysa* and *hâlbuki* open a contradicting clause; *buna rağmen* is **despite this**; *gerçi … ama* is **granted …, but**.
